owner_instruction_excerpt: Yes redraft. For ram and cpu I want to provide a cap that protects hermes but leaves enough resources for other development processes

owner_overrides.overridden: Agent's review framing, which assessed the source document against DIAL's locked model-runtime chain, development gate and knowledge-layer provenance.
owner_overrides.ruling: The document governs execution venue only. Model selection and any single project's development policy are a different layer and do not belong in it.
owner_overrides.effect: Rev 2 declares model selection and project development policy explicitly out of scope, and interfaces with project runtime policy only as a subordinate.

owner_overrides.overridden: Agent's proposal to replace the locality_reason enum with an enumerated PROVIDER_INSUFFICIENT_<REASON> taxonomy.
owner_overrides.ruling: No list of jobs that may run on the VM. If a provider can handle the work with the infrastructure its subscription allows, it does it there; Oracle is used only when provider infrastructure is inadequate.
owner_overrides.effect: All pre-dispatch allowlists are removed. Venue is decided by attempting the work in the provider and observing the outcome. The observed reason is recorded as audit evidence and nothing branches on it.

owner_overrides.overridden: Agent's treatment of dial-* naming as evidence of single-project coupling.
owner_overrides.ruling: DIAL is the company name. Naming does not tie infrastructure to one project; infrastructure must be separable from any single project.
owner_overrides.effect: dial-* infrastructure names are retained. Coupling is addressed by removing project content (project truth, knowledge layer, hardcoded repository) into a per-project binding.

owner_overrides.overridden: Agent's open question on whether the A1 downsize was justified.
owner_overrides.ruling: The resize keeps the setup in the free tier, and provider-first utilisation exists to avoid resource pressure.
owner_overrides.effect: Accepted as the stated rationale. The aggregate-allowance question is retained in Open Decisions as a measurement against the live tenancy, not as an objection.

notes: Owner directed a cap that protects the control plane while leaving usable capacity for other development processes. Rev 1 expressed ceilings only, which bound growth but do not prevent a slice being squeezed. Rev 2 pairs a protection floor (MemoryMin/MemoryLow) with a ceiling (MemoryHigh/MemoryMax) per slice, and gives the development slice no MemoryLow so it is reclaimed first.

Owner's stated RAM figure is read as 6 GB and applied as the control-plane MemoryMax. MemoryHigh is set at 5G so reclaim is graceful rather than an abrupt OOM kill, and MemoryMin at 2G is the guaranteed floor that development pressure cannot reclaim.

Owner's 125/200% CPU figures are applied as a steady-state budget and a hard ceiling respectively. systemd has no CPUHigh primitive, so 125% is enforced as an admission-control and alert threshold while 200% is CPUQuota. CPUWeight ordering (survival 10000, control 800, dev 400) is what makes a 200% ceiling safe on a 2 OCPU host, since quota is a ceiling and not a reservation.

Rev 1 asserted a >=3.5 GB survival reserve while its own MemoryMax=7.5G plus a 2.5 GB sandbox left 1.0 GB. Rev 2 restates the reserve as >=3.0 GB at steady state, which the configuration can actually honor, and records the arithmetic.

Antigravity was absent from Rev 1 despite existing in the repository as a provider adapter with a worker identity model. Rev 2 replaces the two hardcoded provider execution classes with a single PROVIDER class resolved against a registry, so adding a provider is a registry change rather than a policy rewrite.

Rev 2 separates provider outage from provider inadequacy. Outage never reaches Oracle; only a provider attempt that ran and failed for an infrastructure cause does. Ambiguous provider signals default to outage because that bias protects the control plane.

Acceptance tests G through K are new and must be proven by inducing the failure. Rev 1 tested only that guards deny what they are asked to deny, never that they cannot be bypassed or that they fail closed.
This is a planning document marked PROPOSED - NOT_IMPLEMENTED. It advances no project gate and is not evidence of a deployed control.

The written path is docs/infrastructure/ only. It does not touch agent-system/orchestration, agent-system/engineering-knowledge or deploy/oracle/hermes-codex, so the control-plane qualification fingerprint is unchanged by this commit.
